# Lamentations 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** How the-Lord has-covered with-a-cloud in-His-anger the-daughter-of Zion! He-has-cast from-heaven to-earth the-beauty-of Israel, and-has-not-remembered His-footstool in-the-day-of His-anger.

**2** The-Lord has-swallowed-up without-pity all the-habitations-of Jacob; He-has-torn-down in-His-fury the-fortifications-of the-daughter-of Judah; He-brought-down to-the-ground — He-profaned the-kingdom and-its-princes.

**3** He-cut-off in-burning anger every horn-of Israel; He-drew-back His-right-hand from-before the-enemy; and-He-burned in-Jacob like-a-fire-of flame [that]-devours all-around.

**4** He-bent His-bow like-an-enemy; He-stationed His-right-hand like-a-foe, and-He-killed all [the]-delights-of [the]-eye in-the-tent-of the-daughter-of Zion; He-poured-out like-fire His-fury.

**5** The-Lord has-become like-an-enemy; He-has-swallowed-up Israel, He-has-swallowed-up all her-palaces, He-has-destroyed his-fortifications; and-He-multiplied in-the-daughter-of Judah mourning and-moaning.

**6** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**7** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**8** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**9** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**10** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**11** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**12** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**13** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**14** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**15** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**16** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**17** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**18** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**19** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**20** And-the-Lord in-His-wrath brought-down the-walls-of Zion and-her-gates sank into-the-ground.

**21** Young and-old lie on-the-ground in-the-streets; my-virgins and-my-young-men fell by-the-sword; You-killed in-the-day-of Your-anger — You-slaughtered without-pity.

**22** You-summoned as-on-a-feast-day my-terrors from-every-side, and-there-was-not in-the-day-of YHWH's anger an-escapee or-a-survivor; those-whom I-nursed and-raised — my-enemy annihilated-them.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **2:1**: Adonai (Lord) — chapter 2 uses Adonai rather than YHWH for the divine subject, emphasizing God's sovereign lordship in judgment. He is explicitly the agent of destruction.

- **2:4**: Darakh qashto ke-oyev — 'He bent His bow like an enemy.' God as archer firing on His own people — the most shocking theological image in the Hebrew Bible.

- **2:22**: Yom mo'ed — 'feast day.' The terrible irony: God 'summons' enemies like invitations to a festival. The sacred calendar is inverted into a calendar of terror.

— EMET
